proof_summary: Writing each binomial ratio from \(p^{m-1}\) to \(p^m\) as \(\beta_t=\prod_{1\le k\le p^m,\,p\nmid k}(1+t p^m/k)\) for \(t=1,2\), the proof uses doubling and reflection of the unit residues to obtain sharp \(p\)-adic bounds for inverse power sums, then Newton identities to expand \(\beta_t\) through degree four with error of valuation at least \(5m-1\). In the decisive combination \(F_2-3F_1+2\), the reflection identities cancel all lower-valuation terms; together with recursively derived Wolstenholme-type bounds for the preceding binomial coefficients, every remaining term has valuation at least \(3m+3\).
